- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.11) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 2–5% for 30d horizon.
- If sentiment dips below 0.06 and price shows recent downward momentum, model often undercorrects; add 1–3% downward bias to forecast.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ above recent high) are common; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak for 30d horizon.
- Mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is >10% above 18d average, adjust down by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- Sentiment +0.11–0.17 with low volatility → model overfits short-term noise; reduce forecast variance by 10–20%.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.28) and price is trending up, model often fails to recognize reversal; reduce forecast slope by 1–2% per day.
- For 30d horizon, if true outcome is consistently 2–4% below forecast, apply 2–5% downward correction to next forecast if sentiment remains neutral or positive.
